recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13455 unless the work group later chooses to consolidate overlapping FHIR-13455 and FHIR-51608 narrative for editorial maintainability.
issue_request: FHIR-13455 was a Published FHIR-core/FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3, asking whether compartment-style URLs such as POST/PUT [base]/Patient/[id]/Condition were valid. The accepted resolution was to explicitly state that POST/PUT to a compartment is undefined and that servers are not expected to support it.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 5d659690848585f07612bd55190eb52f170a8737, matching Jira's svn revision 13035 comment. That commit added narrative to source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml saying read/write responses for compartment-qualified resource URLs are not defined and that servers are not expected to support read or write to such URLs.
additional_context: CompartmentDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml is in current build scope. The current source retains the FHIR-13455 guidance, including the POST example and no-expectation statement. Later Applied issue FHIR-51608 also clarified the same page by stating that search is the only RESTful interaction defined on compartment endpoints and that reads, writes, operations, history, and batch/transaction POSTs are not defined through compartment-qualified URLs. Searches found no relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence that would change this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already satisfies FHIR-13455 and later source changes reinforce rather than contradict the decision.

related_jiras.note: Applied R6 clarification on the same CompartmentDefinition page confirms that only search is defined for compartment endpoints and explicitly covers writes, operations, history, and batch/transaction POSTs. It was used as context, not independently decided.
